title: WeSCE: A Benchmark for Measuring Security Drift in LLM-Driven Code Editing
abstract: arXiv:2608.15092v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In this work, we introduce WeSCE, a benchmark for quantifying security drift in code editing under weak-security constraints, where tasks specify only functional objectives without explicit security requirements. WeSCE consists of 400 executable programs derived from real-world code, covering feature addition, feature removal, bug fixing, and refactoring. To quantify security drift, we propose a continuous risk representation that aggregates heterogeneous vulnerability signals through a unified formulation, and define drift measures capturing changes in overall risk, worst-case severity, and vulnerability distribution under code transformations, providing a multi-scale view of security spanning average-case behavior to worst-case emphasis.

translated_title: WeSCE：一个用于衡量LLM驱动代码编辑中安全漂移的基准
translated_abstract: 在本工作中，我们引入了WeSCE，一个用于量化弱安全约束下代码编辑中安全漂移的基准，其中任务仅指定功能目标，而不包含明确的安全要求。WeSCE包含400个源自真实世界代码的可执行程序，涵盖功能添加、功能移除、错误修复和重构。为了量化安全漂移，我们提出了一种连续风险表示，通过统一公式聚合异构漏洞信号，并定义了漂移度量，用于捕获代码转换下整体风险、最坏情况严重性和漏洞分布的变化，从而提供从平均情况行为到最坏情况重点的多尺度安全视图。
tldr: 本文提出了WeSCE基准和连续风险表示方法，首次系统量化了LLM在代码编辑中因弱安全约束导致的安全漂移，覆盖多种编辑类型并提供多尺度安全评估。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the WeSCE benchmark and a continuous risk representation method, systematically quantifying for the first time security drift in LLM-driven code editing under weak-security constraints, covering multiple edit types and offering multi-scale security assessment.
